# World-best: learning content generated by code during a live lesson

**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Area:** LLM-generated interactive simulations and games, generative UI protocols, auto-diagrams,
programmatic animation, image generation for education, validation and QA of generated content, latency strategies,
sandboxing. · **Question:** what is the best architecture for putting generated content on screen within 2 s while the
lesson continues? · **Status:** a research extension. Nothing here has been run on children, and this session took no
new measurements.

**What this file is NOT.** It does not repeat what Taxila has already researched, decided and in most cases built. Read
these first:
- `content/CONTENT-ENGINE.md`: tiers T0-T3 and the library, 46 engines, bridge v2.1, the teacher observation pipeline.
- `content/genui-reliability.md`: Google Generative UI, Harnessing GenUI for Education (3.5% → 69.3%), Learn Your Way,
  Claude artifacts and v0, `scene@1`, the T1 and T2a benches, the Azure structured-output limits.
- `content/diagrams-images.md`, `content/animation-video.md`, `content/teacher-visual.md`, `content/sandbox-telemetry.md`.
- `factory/FACTORY.md`, `factory/auto-validation-qa.md` (ladder Q0-Q10, GameGen-Verifier, PlaytestArena, GameASG),
  `factory/llm-game-generation.md`, `factory/video-animation-gen.md` (Code2Video, TheoremExplainAgent, ManimTrainer,
  SGA), `factory/asset-pipeline.md` (StylePack, gpt-image-2 references, consistency), `factory/sandboxes-per-student.md`.
- `context/decisions.md`: `content-live-tiers`, `diagram-router-no-baked-labels`, `forge-media-lanes`,
  `forge-qa-ladder`, `forge-g1-live-t1-t2a`, `engines-in-sandbox-frame-v1`.
- `context/rejected.md`: `live-free-generation`, `generated-media-carries-facts`, `sora-for-curriculum`,
  `forge-live-codegen-race`, `per-child-night-pipeline`, `forge-g2-code-gates-miss-pictures`.
- `context/measurements.md`: `forge-g1-turn-path-2026-10-03` (0 model calls on the request path; 0 ms p50 after
  prefetch) and `forge-g1-prefetch-hitrate-2026-10-03` (99% of mountable queue items warmed).

This file adds **evidence published or found since those were written**: the March 2026 product launches, MCP Apps
going Final, A2UI v0.9, and about fifteen 2026 papers on interaction-graph evaluation, GUI playtesting, judge
reliability, knowledge-intensive image generation and speculative agents. It adds three **licence facts that were
open `[U]`**, the **Azure latency levers that exist (and two that do not)**, and a steal list mapped to the shipped
modules (`server/forge/*`, `src/modules/frame/*`, `server/director/modules.js`).

**Tags.** **[V]** read in the primary source this session (abstract, HTML or PDF text, a vendor doc or a licence file;
"abs" means the abstract only). **[S]** secondary (a search summary, the press, or a claim quoted by another source).
**[U]** unverified, or a Taxila design inference that has to be measured. **[T]** confirmed by reading Taxila's own
code or docs this session.

## 0. The answer on one screen

1. **The architecture question is already answered, and the world has converged on Taxila's answer.** Every frontier
   lab that shipped "generated interactive learning content" in 2026 shipped one of two things. Some shipped **curated,
   parameterised modules**: ChatGPT's interactive learning has "more than 70 concepts" with tweakable variables
   (2026-03-10) [S]. Others shipped **slow free code, with no reliability claim**: Claude's inline visuals (2026-03-12,
   HTML+JS calling Chart.js, D3 or Plotly, beta) [V blog + S]; Gemini dynamic view and AI Mode (Nov 2025, "a minute or
   two" per page per the Generative UI paper) [V]; Gemini app "simulations and models" (2026-08-24, Pro model,
   "usage limits apply") [V]. None of them publishes a correctness rate. The protocol world went the same way.
   **A2UI** (Google, Apache-2.0, v0.9.1, v1.0 RC) is "safe like data, but expressive like code": a flat list of
   catalogue components, no executable code [V]. **MCP Apps** (Final 2026-01-26, adopted by Claude, ChatGPT and
   VS Code) runs HTML only in a double-iframe sandbox with a deny-by-default CSP [V]. Taxila's rule (models fill
   data, tested code renders, grades and animates) is the world's best practice. It is no longer a conservative bet.
2. **The 2 s budget is not a model-speed problem. On the planned path it is already solved: measured, 0 ms after the
   lesson-start prefetch, with 0/69 model calls on the request path** [T: `forge-g1-turn-path`]. The open problem is the
   **off-plan request**: the child asks something, the teacher detours, a misconception fires. There the honest
   numbers are T1 at 1.88 s p50 and T2a at 3.08 s p50, and **1.29 s of the T1 wall time is service overhead, not
   tokens** [T: genui §3.2]. The best architecture for that path is in §2 and steals S1-S5. **Skeleton first, words
   streamed, no model on the critical path when a code fill exists, and speculative launches that only mount on
   commit.**
3. **Behaviour, not looks, is where generated interactives fail, and 2026 measured it more sharply.**
   - InteractScience (150 science demos): the best model passes **every** test on only **13.29%** of tasks. Logic and
     scientific errors cause 53% of failures; widgets "work" while "visual states still violated the intended
     scientific semantics" [V].
   - WebRISE (442 tasks): one model scored **80.8% visual but 15.5% functional** [V abs].
   - GameASG-Bench: a mean of 93.2% of checks passes while only **55.3%** of tasks pass all checks [V].

   **Report strict all-checks pass rates, never means** (S6, anti-pattern A3).
4. **Interactivity is best evaluated as a state graph. `scene@1` already *is* one.** EE-Eval extracts a finite-state
   machine from generated explorable explanations and compares it with an ideal pedagogical FSM. It reaches r = 0.728
   with human interactivity ratings, against **0.530 for a VLM judge and −0.600 for unit tests** [V]. WebRISE's
   "interaction contract graphs" find state errors at 2-16x the rate of checkpoint tests [V abs]. Taxila's solver
   already enumerates reachable states. The missing piece is an **ideal graph per template or archetype**, so that
   promotion can check the *shape* of the interaction and not only that the goals are reachable (S6).
5. **Holistic VLM judges are now measured as unreliable. Checklist judges are not.**
   - ManimAgent: VLM score vs human, **Pearson r = −0.17** [V].
   - SciDraw-Bench: GPT-4o vs Gemini inter-judge r = 0.58-0.63 [V].
   - WebDevJudge (ICLR 2026): the best judge reaches 70.3% pairwise agreement, against 84.6% for humans [S].
   - KVBench: **binary atomic checklist items** judged by Qwen2.5-VL reach **κ = 0.745** with experts [V].

   Taxila's "VLM checklist with a code verdict" (`forge-qa-ladder`) is right. Holistic "rate this 1-10" calls must
   never gate anything (S9, A2).
6. **Pixels still cannot carry curriculum facts.** On KVBench (1,800 prompts from 30+ textbooks, six school subjects)
   the best text-to-image model scores **51.4% overall** (Gemini-3-pro-image) and **36.3% at best on mathematics** [V].
   SciDraw-Bench's best general model reaches text fidelity 0.61 [V]. This independently confirms
   `generated-media-carries-facts`. Nothing new reverses it.
7. **The best repair loops in 2026 use negative memory.** ManimAgent's "negative channel" stores validated failure
   patterns as **hard constraints**. It halved reflection rounds (12.2 → 6.5) and raised human pass@1 from 62.0% to
   84.9% [V]. Forge already writes its failures down in `rejected.md` and the G2 QA logs. It does not yet feed them
   back to the builder as constraints (S8).
8. **Geometry and diagrams: declarative constraints beat constructive code.** LLMs fail to write Penrose's
   constructive Substance/Style programs even with human help. MagicGeo's declarative constraints plus a solver work
   [S]. GeoSVG-RL makes the model emit a **layout plan as a "geometric contract"** before any SVG, and rewards it from
   a browser verifier (anchors, text-in-box, canvas fit) [V abs]. GeoBuildBench finds that models "struggle to exploit
   visual and constraint-based feedback for self-correction" [V abs]. This is the design for the offline
   `svg-figure@1` and `geo-construct@1` lanes (S10).
9. **Licence facts that were `[U]` are now settled** (S11):
   - **JSXGraph** is dual LGPL-3.0+ / **MIT** (the repo README) [V], so `geo-construct@1` can be built on it under MIT.
   - **GeoGebra** states that "any use … for a commercial purpose … requires a special license" (the source code is
     EUPL, but the apps and services are non-commercial) [V]. Do not embed it.
   - The **Desmos API** needs an API key, and partnership terms are negotiated [V doc]. The ToS page did not render
     [U]. Do not depend on it.
   - **GSAP**, all plugins included, is free for commercial use. The one banned use is tools that let *users* "build
     visual animations without code" in competition with Webflow [V]. A teacher-facing animation editor would need a
     legal read.
10. **Azure latency levers: two that exist, two that do not.**
    - **Exists: priority processing** (`service_tier: priority`, target 99% > 80 TPS for gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-6-sol).
      **It does not list gpt-5.6-luna (`taxila-fast`)** [V Learn, 2026-09-22]. Luna already decodes at about 250 TPS
      (4 ms/token [T]). Priority therefore helps only the brain/sol lanes (near-line T2b and repairs), and traffic that
      ramps more than 50% in 15 minutes is silently downgraded to standard [V].
    - **Exists: the asynchronous content filter** for streaming, which removes filter buffering [S Learn]. It is safe
      for Taxila only because no streamed text reaches a child before Taxila's own Q8 gate.
    - **Does not exist: predicted outputs.** Azure lists only gpt-4o / 4.1-family models [S Learn], so a scene cannot
      be "edited by prediction" on our deployments.
    - **Does not exist: client-side speculative decoding** on hosted Azure models. Speculation has to happen at the
      **action** level (S5).

## 1. Landscape: who does what better than anyone (2024-2026)

### 1.1 Products shipping generated or parameterised learning visuals

| product (date) | what it does better than anyone | how it is built | reliability evidence | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ChatGPT interactive learning** (2026-03-10) | Scale with zero visible failure. 70+ maths and science concepts (Pythagoras, Coulomb's law, lens equation) where the learner changes variables or the formula and the graph updates live | It reads as curated parameterised modules ("more than 70 concepts", more "down the line"); OpenAI's page returned 403 | none published; 140 M weekly maths/science learners (the press) | [S] |
| **Claude custom visuals in chat** (2026-03-12, beta) | Visuals that are **ephemeral and conversational**: they "change or disappear as discussions evolve", unlike artifacts. Claude decides when a visual helps | HTML/CSS/JS inline, using Chart.js / D3 / Plotly via CDN (the press); the blog gives no technical detail | none published | [V blog, S tech] |
| **Gemini dynamic view / visual layout; AI Mode generative UI** (2025-11) | The broadest free generation: whole interactive pages for any prompt | Gemini 3 plus a long system prompt and nine post-processors (genui §1) | 82.8% preferred to markdown; "a minute or two" per page; errors 29-60% on the weaker tiers | [V paper] |
| **Gemini app "simulations and models"** (2026-08-24) | Rotatable 3D molecules and physics systems (a pendulum's energy exchange) in chat | Pro model; "usage limits apply" | none published | [V] |
| **Project Genie / Genie 3** (2026-01-29, Ultra) | Real-time playable worlds at 720p/24 fps from a prompt | an 11B autoregressive world model; consistency for "several minutes" | there is no state to assert against, so nothing can be graded | [S] |

**Read-across.** Everyone who ships to *learners at scale without an adult in the loop* (ChatGPT) ships curated
modules. Free generation ships where an adult iterates (Claude, Gemini). That is Taxila's T0/T1 vs T3 split, and no
product has shown a third way.

### 1.2 Protocols for agent-generated UI (new since genui §1)

| protocol | what it does better than anyone | details that matter to Taxila | tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A2UI** (Google, 2025-12-15; v0.9.1 current, v1.0 RC; Apache-2.0) | Cross-platform generative UI as **pure data**. The client keeps a "catalog of trusted, pre-approved UI components"; the agent can only reference them | A flat component list with ID references, "LLM-optimized" for **incremental, progressive rendering**. Renderers: Lit, Flutter, Angular (React, Compose and SwiftUI on the roadmap). Transport over A2A or AG-UI | [V blog + repo] |
| **MCP Apps** (SEP-1865, Final 2026-01-26; Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Goose) | The first cross-vendor standard for sandboxed HTML views | **Double iframe:** an outer sandbox proxy on a different origin, then the inner view with a strict CSP built from declared `connectDomains` / `resourceDomains` (deny by default). JSON-RPC over postMessage. **`ui/notifications/tool-input-partial`** streams partial arguments ("best-effort recovery with auto-closed brackets") before `tool-input`. Tool **`visibility: ["app"]`** gives tools the view can call but the model never sees. Host CSS variables for theme. `ui/update-model-context` lets the view write to the model's context | [V spec] |
| **json-render** (Vercel Labs, 2026) | A guardrailed catalogue in zod, streamed progressive rendering across React, Vue, Svelte and React Native | Same pattern as A2UI; 36 shadcn components | [S] |

**Read-across.** `scene@1` (22 primitives, a flat A2UI-style list, a solver) is already stricter than A2UI. A2UI
validates component membership but not the *meaning* of an interaction. Taxila's bridge v2.1 (facts of ≤ 12 primitive
keys, the host grades) is stricter than MCP Apps, whose `ui/update-model-context` would let a view write free text into
the model's context. Taxila must never adopt that (A7). Two ideas are worth taking: **partial-input streaming into a
mounted view** (S1) and **app-only tools** (S1 note).

| **EE-Eval** (Wang, Wang & Wen, 2026-06-30, arXiv 2606.31012) | Evaluates interactivity as an **FSM**: it extracts the state machine from generated explorable explanations (few-shot LLM extraction) and compares it with an ideal pedagogical FSM using graph and embedding metrics; thousands of artefacts, 127 concepts, 6 models | human alignment on interactivity r = **0.728**, VLM 0.530, unit tests **−0.600**; the best generator is GPT-5 Mini at 78.9% FSM similarity. ## 2. The best architecture for generation inside 2 s while the lesson continues

**Principle.** The child must never wait on a model. The teacher's voice covers about 2-3 s of preamble, and the
module mounts **frozen** until `your_turn` (genui §3.2) [T]. So the target is *time to first meaningful paint ≤ 300 ms*
and *time to interactive ≤ the end of the preamble*, with everything that carries truth coming from code.

```
                            Director move (planned queue)           off-plan want (child question / detour / misc signal)
                                     |                                        |
   L0  PREFETCH (exists)   lesson-start planned prefetch, 99% of        S5 speculative launch from partial tool args
                           mountable queue items warm; 0 ms p50 [T]     (commit-on-match, never mounts unless chosen)
                                     |                                        |
   L1  CODE-ONLY FILL      template + kit + strings table, no model    S2: every T1/T2a slot has a code value
       (<= 100 ms)         (G1 ships code picks today, `no_time`) [T]   (ask templates per probe kind x lang)
                                     |                                        |
   L2  SKELETON-FIRST      S1: mount the code skeleton frozen; stream language slots; each string passes Q8 before
       MOUNT (<= 300 ms)   it is painted; interaction unlocks only after lint + solver on the final document
                                     |
   L3  MODEL UPGRADE       background flavour / language upgrade into the cache (exists for G1) [T];
       (async)             S3 token diet + S4 service-overhead cuts bring a live T2a model fill under 2 s p90
                                     |
   L4  NEAR-LINE (>=45 s)  free scene@1 (T2b) on brain/sol with priority processing (S4); cached; promoted after review
   L5  OFFLINE FORGE       T3 games/sims: declared test seam, state-injection keypoints, interaction-graph gate (S6),
                           GUI playtester advisory (S7), negative-memory builder (S8), checklist judges (S9), two-key review
```

What is new in this picture compared with CONTENT-ENGINE §1:
- **L2 is new.** Today a T2a fill is shown when it is complete. Streaming *into a mounted, frozen skeleton* is how
  A2UI, json-render and MCP Apps hide latency [V]. Taxila can do it more safely, because the skeleton's geometry and
  truth fields are code and never stream.
- **L0's speculation is new.** Prefetch covers the *planned* queue. Action speculation (§1.3 of the speculative-agent
  papers, S5) covers what the teacher is about to ask for.
- **L1 becomes a guarantee, not an optimisation.** "No model on the critical path" is already measured for G1 (0/69)
  [T]. S2 extends it to every live tier, so the model is *only ever* an upgrade.

## 3. STEAL LIST (ranked by expected impact per unit of work)

Every item names the files it touches, the expected impact, how to measure it, and its licence and compliance
constraints. All runtime stays on Azure: `taxila-fast` (gpt-5.6-luna), `taxila-brain` (gpt-5.6-sol),
`taxila-codex`, ACA.

### S1. Skeleton-first progressive mount for live T2a/T1 fills (from A2UI, json-render and MCP Apps `tool-input-partial`)
- **Mechanism.** When a fill is not in cache, the server sends the **code-derived skeleton** at once: the template id,
  every truth-bearing field (operands, options' values, correct id, order, traps from `server/forge/derive.js`), and
  geometry from the scene layout port. The frame mounts it **frozen**, with text slots shown as neutral placeholders
  (shapes, never words). The model's language slots then stream. Each slot is painted only after it passes the
  per-string Q8 gate (`server/forge/gate.js`). The probe unlocks only when the whole document has passed lint and the
  solver (`server/forge/scene/dsl.mjs`), exactly as today.
- **Files.** `server/forge/index.js` (`requestFill` returns `{skeleton, slotsPending}` then `slot` events);
  `src/modules/frame/protocol.ts` (new host→frame `fill_partial {slot, value}`, seq-ordered, ≤ 8 KiB); 
  `src/modules/frame/scene/runtime.ts` (placeholder slots; the probe stays disabled until `fill_final`);
  `shared/forge.ts` (types).
- **Impact.** The off-plan first paint goes from 1.9-3.1 s to ≤ 300 ms [U]. The visible-latency share of off-plan
  turns falls by roughly the T2a wall time.
- **Measure.** A new `evals/forge-live-partial.mjs` reports time to first paint, time to interactive and the count of
  strings blocked mid-stream, on the 8 genui-bench briefs and the 23-turn G1 sample, from centralindia and eastus2.
  Gate: TTFP p90 ≤ 300 ms, TTI p90 ≤ 3.0 s, 0 ungated strings painted (a seeded unsafe-slot control must never paint).
- **Constraints.** No new licence. Safety: a placeholder must never be a word, and a slot that fails Q8 makes the whole
  fill fall back to the code value (S2), never to an empty card. **Do not** adopt MCP Apps' `ui/update-model-context`
  (A7). *Note:* MCP's `visibility:["app"]` matches Taxila's split between module-callable and voice-callable tools.
  Keep tools the voice model can call to the two realtime tools (CONTENT-ENGINE §1.6).

### S2. Every live slot has a code value: the model becomes an upgrade, never a dependency
- **Mechanism.** Extend G1's "code pick ships now, model pick upgrades the cache" (`no_time`, measured) [T] to the
  T1 `ask` and every T2a language slot. Build per-template, per-probe-kind `ask` templates in `en`, `hi` and `hi_latn`
  in `server/forge/strings.js`, filled with kit nouns and numbers. genui §3.2 already proposes this ("Even the `ask`
  can be templated per probe kind, leaving no model call at all") [T]. The model call then runs only to *improve* the
  wording into the cache.
- **Files.** `server/forge/strings.js`, `server/forge/templates.js`, `server/forge/generator.js`,
  `server/forge/index.js`.
- **Impact.** Off-plan latency for T1 and T2a drops to the code path (≤ 100 ms server-side [U]). The remaining risk
  is a stiffer phrasing on the first encounter only.
- **Measure.** "Model calls on the request path" stays 0/N across all live tiers (the G1 metric, extended). A blind
  rating of code `ask` vs model `ask` (n ≥ 40 per language, class teacher raters) for naturalness and clarity. Reverse
  if code asks are rated clearly worse *and* children's first-attempt rates drop on them.
- **Constraints.** The strings table keeps the Q8 allow-list property: every visible string is a kit string, a table
  string or a template constant. Sentence-shaped text in prompts is recited, but this is *child-facing UI copy*, not
  prompt text, so it is the right place for sentences.

### S3. Token diet for live fills: one language, no nulls, optionally a Lark line DSL
- **Mechanism.** Output tokens are the engine-side budget at 4 ms/token [T]. Three cuts:
  1. Generate **only the lesson's active language**. Today the `ask` is `{en, hi, hi_latn}`, roughly triple the
     tokens; Devanagari tokenises worse than Latin [U].
  2. Ship `scene@1.1`'s smaller optional surface, since **24.5% of the strict payload is `null`** [T].
  3. Try the reversal condition already written for `dsl-strict-decoding`: a Lark CFG line DSL, which Azure accepts
     at 1.0-1.4 s [T].
- **Files.** `docs/research/content/genui-scene-dsl.mjs` (v1.4 optional-field pruning), `server/forge/scene/dsl.mjs`,
  `server/forge/generator.js`.
- **Impact.** T2a from about 380 to about 150-200 output tokens, roughly −0.7 to −0.9 s engine time [U]. A live T2a
  fill could then land at p90 ≤ 2.4 s.
- **Measure.** Re-run `content/genui-bench.mjs` T2a arms (n = 8 briefs × 3 runs) on: the current schema; one language;
  1.1 pruned; Lark. Report output tokens, p50/p90 and lint-clean on the first call. Adopt an arm only if validity does
  not drop.
- **Constraints.** None beyond the existing strict-decoding rule.

### S4. Attack the 1.29 s service overhead, and use priority processing only where it exists
- **Mechanism.** On T1, 0.90 s is engine time and 1.29 s is "service" [T]. Candidates, each to be measured, not
  assumed:
  - **Region.** Measure an India-region deployment (southindia supports priority processing for sol models [V]; luna
    availability is to be checked) against eastus2 from an Indian client.
  - **Connection reuse.** Keep-alive / HTTP/2 from `server/azure.js`, so no request pays a TLS handshake.
  - **Content-filter mode.** Try the asynchronous filter on streamed fills [S]. It is safe because S1 paints nothing
    before Q8, and Q8 includes per-string Content Safety plus the Hinglish blocklist (`forge-qa-ladder`).
  - **Priority processing.** Use `service_tier: "priority"` **only on sol/brain lanes** (near-line T2b, repairs, the
    critic). It does not list luna [V].
  - **Smooth the ramp.** The 18:00 IST peak can exceed the "+50% TPM in 15 min" ramp and get downgraded silently [V].
    Read `service_tier` in each response and log it.
- **Files.** `server/azure.js` (agent keep-alive, `service_tier`, response-tier logging),
  `docs/research/models/MODEL-ROUTER.md`, the deploy scripts for the deployment's filter policy.
- **Impact.** −0.3 to −1.0 s on every live model call [U]; a tighter p90 on near-line lanes.
- **Measure.** A 2×2×2 latency matrix (region × keep-alive × filter mode), n = 30 each, T1 fill, reported as wall and
  server-timing split. For priority: the T2b p50/p90 at 18:00-21:30 IST on default vs priority, and the downgrade rate.
- **Constraints.** All Azure. The filter-mode change may need a modified content-filtering approval [U]. The
  child-safety floor is unchanged because Taxila's own gate is the blocking layer (`content-safety-sole-gate`).

### S5. Speculative module launch, committed only on match (from Speculative Actions, SPORK and PASTE)
- **Mechanism.** The agent literature (2025-2026) speculates on *actions*: predict the next tool call, launch it, and
  commit only if the real call matches. That is lossless when side effects are reversible [V abs: Speculative Actions:
  up to 55% next-action accuracy, up to 20% latency cut; S: SPORK tool-name prediction 74.6-99.6%]. In Taxila the side
  effect is a cache entry, so it is fully reversible. Three triggers:
  1. The realtime voice model's tool call: start the fill on the **first parsed field** of a partial `want`
     (`mechanic`) rather than on the completed call.
  2. A misconception signal from `server/comprehension/*`: pre-fill that misconception's contrast probe.
  3. A child question routed to "show": pre-fill the top 2 renderers from the diagram router.

  None of these mount unless the Director chooses them (`prefetch:true`, "not shown until chosen", CONTENT-ENGINE §1.6)
  [T].
- **Files.** `server/director/modules.js`, `server/forge/planner.js`, `server/forge/cache.js`, the realtime tool
  handler in `server/routes/*` (lesson tool route).
- **Impact.** It converts part of the off-plan traffic into prefetch hits [U]. The cost is bounded because L1 code fills
  cost no model tokens.
- **Measure.** Speculation hit rate (fills launched / fills mounted), wasted model tokens per lesson, and off-plan
  visible latency, from `evals/director-sim.mjs` traces plus 20 real lesson logs. Budget gate: wasted model spend
  ≤ 10% of the lesson's model spend.
- **Constraints.** Respect `prefetch_invalidate` and `lm_seq` (CONTENT-ENGINE §1.6.5). Anything child-dependent stays
  out of child-free caches (`forge-g1-child-name-in-cached-gate`).

### S6. An interaction-graph promotion gate, with strict all-checks scoring (from EE-Eval, WebRISE and GameASG)
- **Mechanism.** For every template (`choice-card@1`, `sequence-steps@1`, `sort-bins@1`, …) and every tgk@1
  archetype, author an **ideal pedagogical FSM**: states (frozen, predict-committed, exploring, probe-answered-wrong
  with the misconception id, reveal) and transitions. The `scene@1` solver already enumerates reachable states. Export
  that reachable graph and compare it with the ideal: every ideal transition present; no shortcut edge from mount to
  `goal_met` (the remove-the-learning test); trap edges labelled with kit misconception ids. For T3 games, extract the
  graph from `__forge` snapshots under the bot. **Score strictly** (all required transitions present) and report mean
  coverage only as a diagnostic.
- **Files.** `docs/research/content/genui-scene-dsl.mjs` (solver graph export), `server/forge/scene/dsl.mjs`, a new
  `server/forge/g2/graph.js`, `server/forge/g2/qa.js`, `tests/scene-runtime.test.mjs`.
- **Impact.** Catches "works but teaches the wrong interaction" (InteractScience's 53% logic errors; the flower
  squeezed into sort-bins in genui §0.7, which no validator caught) before human review. The reviewers' reject rate on
  promoted T2b/T3 should fall [U].
- **Measure.** Seed 20 defective scenes and 10 defective G2 builds (missing reveal, a shortcut to `goal_met`, an
  unlabelled trap, a wrong-template fit). Recall ≥ 0.9 and 0 false rejects on the 47 existing positive controls. Then
  track the human-review reject rate for 4 weeks.
- **Constraints.** EE-Eval extracts FSMs with an LLM because free HTML hides them. Taxila must **not** do that: the
  graph comes from the solver and the seam (code), so it is exact.

### S7. A GUI-agent playtester as an advisory offline gate, with trajectory-conditioned diagnosis (PlaytestArena + DiagEval)
- **Mechanism.** After the blocking keypoint state-injection gate (GameGen-Verifier style, `forge-qa-ladder`), run a
  GUI agent (`taxila-brain` vision, Playwright on ACA) that plays the T3 build against the archetype's 5-11 rubric
  behaviours. When it fails, do **not** retry from scratch. Re-probe from the failed trajectory (DiagEval) to decide
  between "the agent fumbled" and "the build is broken". Its findings go to the reviewer and the repair loop; it never
  passes or fails a build on its own.
- **Files.** `server/forge/g2/qa.js`, `server/forge/render-check.mjs`, `server/forge/g2/harness.js`.
- **Impact.** Surfaces unresponsive controls and missing transitions that code inspection misses [V], at κ ≈ human-
  human. DiagEval's +8-17 pp accuracy comes from re-probing [V abs].
- **Measure.** On the G2 mutant set (`forge-g2-bot-without-remove` lineage, 43 mutants): mutants found by the playtester
  that the bot missed, and false defects with and without re-probe. Exclude timing-sensitive archetypes, where it is
  known to fail.
- **Constraints.** Azure-only vision (`taxila-brain`). The survey's warning applies: a judge from the same family as the
  builder shares its blind spots [V abs]. Prefer a different first-party family for the second opinion (S9).

### S8. A negative-memory builder: validated failure patterns as hard constraints, placed last (ManimAgent ℳ⁻)
- **Mechanism.** Every confirmed G2 QA failure (gate, critic or reviewer reject) becomes a structured pitfall:
  `{archetype, symptom, check_id, rule}`. Examples: "hand-drawn partition beside a fraction", "ref.slot read",
  "title clipped at left edge" (`forge-g2-code-gates-miss-pictures`, `forge-g2-refs-carry-slot`). Retrieve the top-k
  pitfalls by archetype and template and append them **last** in the builder brief. Position is mechanism. Write them
  as shapes, not sentences, because sentence-shaped text gets recited. Pitfalls with a code check go in the lint;
  the memory holds only those that cannot be coded.
- **Files.** `server/forge/g2/brief.js`, `server/forge/g2/design.js`, `server/forge/g2/review.js` (writes pitfalls on
  reject), a new `data/forge/pitfalls.json` (versioned, human-approved entries only).
- **Impact.** ManimAgent: rounds to green 12.2 → 6.5 and pass@1 +23 pp [V]. Forge's cost per build and its
  `triage` rate should fall [U].
- **Measure.** An A/B on the next 16 G2 builds, 8 with pitfalls and 8 without: rounds to green, $ per build,
  reviewer rejects.
- **Constraints.** Only human-validated pitfalls (ManimAgent gates memory writes). Never store child data in it.

### S9. Judges: atomic binary checklists, a code verdict, a cross-family second opinion; never holistic scores
- **Mechanism.** Re-audit every VLM/LLM judge call in `server/forge/g2/critic.js` and the asset VLM gate. Each must be
  a list of **atomic yes/no checks** derived from the spec (KVBench-style 4-6 items per target: entity present,
  attribute, spatial relation, outcome), with the verdict computed by code. A holistic score is a diagnostic only. Add a
  second judge from a different Azure-direct family on disagreement-prone checks.
- **Files.** `server/forge/g2/critic.js`, `docs/research/factory/asset-vlm-gate-probe.mjs` lineage, `server/forge/
  render-check.mjs`.
- **Impact.** Taxila's own `generated-media-carries-facts` probe showed the OCR "spelling gate" reading what it
  expects [T]. The 2026 numbers (r = −0.17 holistic; κ = 0.745 checklist) say the checklist form is the only one worth
  keeping [V].
- **Measure.** Per check, judge-vs-human agreement on 60 labelled renders (Cohen's κ). Drop or demote any check with
  κ < 0.6 to reviewer-only.
- **Constraints.** Azure-direct models only. "Which second family" is a router bake-off question
  (`models/MODEL-ROUTER.md`), not a guess.

### S10. Offline exact figures: a layout plan as contract, then a solver and a browser verifier (GeoSVG-RL, MagicGeo, GeoBuildBench)
- **Mechanism.** For `svg-figure@1` and `geo-construct@1` (offline, `diagram-router-no-baked-labels`), the model
  writes a **declarative constraint program**, not coordinates and not SVG. Example: `triangle ABC; angle(A)=60;
  |AB|=5; M midpoint BC; label(A,"A") outside`. A solver places the points (JSXGraph under MIT, or our own numeric
  solver). A headless browser verifies the GeoSVG checks: render validity, canvas fit, anchors, text-in-box, no
  overlaps, and every assertion in the manifest within tolerance. The model repairs from verifier messages at most
  2 times. GeoBuildBench says models use feedback poorly, so then hand off to a human.
- **Files.** The diagram router (CONTENT-ENGINE §6), a new `server/forge/figure/` (constraint IR, solver, verifier),
  `src/modules/frame/engines/geo-construct*` when built.
- **Impact.** Stops the "13/19/148 deg triangle with the right labels" class (`live-free-generation`) by
  construction [T].
- **Measure.** 40 NCERT class 6-9 geometry figures: % exact on the first pass and after 2 repairs; human-review reject
  rate; generation time (offline, so the bound is $ not s).
- **Constraints.** JSXGraph MIT (choose the MIT side of the dual licence and keep its notice) [V]. **No GeoGebra**
  (commercial licence) [V] and **no Desmos** (key plus negotiated terms) [V/U].

### S11. Small items
- **Licence register.** Record JSXGraph (MIT, chosen), GeoGebra (excluded) and Desmos (excluded) in
  `docs/research/content/CONTENT-ENGINE.md` §2, replacing the `[U]` tags. GSAP: the one prohibited use is an end-user
  no-code animation builder. Flag that before any teacher or parent authoring tool ships.
- **Sequential anchoring for multi-figure lessons** (EduIllustrate +13% consistency at −94% cost) [V abs]. When the
  near-line or offline lane makes several figures for one lesson, pass the first approved figure's spec (palette,
  label positions, object ids) as the anchor for the rest (`factory/asset-pipeline.md` StylePack extension).
- **Ephemeral visuals (Claude's pattern).** A board visual that is not a probe may be shown and discarded with no
  library promotion. It still comes only from the diagram router's templates.

## 4. Anti-patterns the field learned the hard way

| # | anti-pattern | evidence | Taxila status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | **Free code on a child's live path** | Gemini pages take "a minute or two"; InteractScience 13.29% all-pass; WebRISE 80.8% visual vs 15.5% functional; Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini publish no correctness rate | rejected (`live-free-generation`); world practice now agrees |
| A2 | **Holistic VLM or LLM scores as a gate** | ManimAgent r = −0.17; SciDraw inter-judge 0.58-0.63; WebDevJudge 70% vs 85% human; EE-Eval VLM 0.53 | partly guarded (`forge-qa-ladder` code verdict); audit in S9 |
| A3 | **Reporting mean check pass rates** | GameASG 93.2% mean vs 55.3% strict | adopt strict in every Forge report (S6) |
| A4 | **Unit tests as a proxy for interaction quality** | EE-Eval: unit testing correlates **−0.600** with human interactivity ratings | keep unit tests for correctness; interaction quality comes from the graph gate (S6) |
| A5 | **Pixels, video or world models as carriers of facts** | KVBench best 51%, maths ≤ 36%; SciDraw text fidelity ≤ 0.61; Genie 3 has no assertable state | rejected (`generated-media-carries-facts`, `sora-for-curriculum`) |
| A6 | **Asking LLMs for constructive diagram programs** (Penrose-style) | LLMs fail even with human help; declarative constraints work (MagicGeo); feedback is poorly used (GeoBuildBench) | S10 |
| A7 | **Letting a view write into the model's context** | MCP Apps `ui/update-model-context` exists and is legitimate for adult tools | never for Taxila: bridge facts only, ≤ 12 primitive keys, never sentences (CONTENT-ENGINE §0.1.6) |
| A8 | **Retrying a GUI-agent evaluation from scratch** | DiagEval: re-probing from the failed trajectory recovers 46-62% of false defects | S7 |
| A9 | **Same-family judge as "independent" evidence** | the Agentic Artifact Creation survey | S9 second family |
| A10 | **Assuming a vendor latency tier covers your model** | Azure priority processing omits luna; the ramp rule downgrades silently; predicted outputs only on 4o/4.1 | S4 logs `service_tier`; do not design on predicted outputs |
| A11 | **Embedding "free" maths tools without reading the licence** | GeoGebra's non-commercial clause; PhET CC BY-NC since 2026-03-29 (already in science-engines) | S11 register |
| A12 | **Long agentic loops presented as interactive** | ManimAgent 19-31 min per animation even when it works | live = templates; loops are offline (`forge-media-lanes`) |
